subject: Qualification debrief: model delta & safeguards
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@novatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Qualification debrief: model delta & safeguards

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for your time on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Use case: extracting financial counterparties and balances from unstructured statements for downstream reconciliation. Primary concern is precision for ENTITY extraction (GL accounts, counterparty names) and a low hallucination rate for numeric fields.
- Target SLOs you mentioned: latency P95 <= 200ms, precision >= 95% on named entities for top-5 entities.

What I’m sending next (by EOD): an eval packet tailored to the dataset you shared, plus a recommended model shortlist and a prompt-set tuned to your label schema.

Questions / asks for you:
1) Can you confirm the anonymized sample corpus link (DevOps shared) is the final dataset we should run against?
2) Are there any hard constraints on tokenization (you mentioned 4k max per request earlier)?
3) Would you prefer a canary rollout (10% traffic) or a staged shadow run first?

I’ll include a short note about our rollback and pinning options — we’ve seen a couple of cases where a minor model version update produced measurable entity-drop deltas, so we’d recommend a guarded approach.

Planned deliverables:
- bespoke eval CSV (entity-level metrics, NER F1, hallucination rate)
- prompt set (JSON) tuned to your labels
- short playbook with pin/rollback steps and canary config

Would it be helpful if Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (model ops) joined a 30-min tech call tomorrow to walk the artifacts?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: (will follow)

From: Aisha Patel <aisha@novatech.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@novatech.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification debrief: model delta & safeguards

Thanks, Sean —

Appreciate the recap. Confirming the anonymized sample live in our shared s3 link is the one to use (https://s3.amazonaws.com/novatech-sample/corpus-2027-04-12.zip). A couple clarifications:

- Hallucination definition: any non-verifiable numeric output or invented counterparty not present in the statement should be flagged.
- We can tolerate brief spikes above 200ms for single large documents, but P95 needs to stay under 200ms.
- Trial window: we’d like to see a two-week proof-of-concept with actual traffic routing if possible.

Regarding pinning/rollback: we need clear SLAs for rollback — if quality drops >2% absolute on the F1 metric, we require an automatic fallback to the previous pinned model. Can you outline how that would work operationally?

Also, please include any SOC2/compliance documents relevant for our security review — we’ll run this through procurement.

—Aisha
Aisha Patel
Head of Data Products | Novatech Industries
aisha@novatech.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@novatech.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 17:02:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification debrief: model delta & safeguards

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear asks. I’m attaching the eval artifacts and a concise set of recommendations below. Attachments: novatech-eval-benchmarks-20270421.csv, prompt-set-novatech-v1.json, rollback-playbook.pdf.

Executive recommendations (shortlist):
1) Llama-Redwood-3-13B-int8 (recommended start): good tradeoff for throughput + entity precision, P95 latency typically ~120–160ms on our Dedicated nodes for similar payloads.
2) Llama-Redwood-3-70B-quant (higher accuracy): expect ~3–5% higher NER F1 on complex PDFs but higher token cost and P95 closer to 220–280ms depending on batch.
3) Baseline fallback: Llama-2-Chat-13B-int8 — stable, predictable latency, slightly lower entity recall but robust to malformed input.

What we ran for the attached evals:
- Synthetic runs on a holdout of your corpus (5k docs) across model variants above. The CSV columns include: model, model_version, dataset_slice, NER_F1, precision, recall, hallucination_rate, avg_latency_p95_ms.
- Observed delta: when we compared Redwood-3 v1.3 -> v1.4 variants during internal regressions, we saw an average absolute drop of 3.8% NER_F1 on ledger-like docs and a small uptick in hallucination_rate (+1.4 percentage points). That delta is the type of regression we want to guard against here.

Pinning and rollback options (operational):
- Pin model version at customer-level: you can pin to a model_version string (e.g., redwood-llama3-13b-int8-1.3.0). Pinning prevents auto-upgrades and ensures requests route to the exact artifact.
- Canary rollout: configured via Redwood Console -> route policies. Example: canary: {"percent": 10, "duration": "72h", "monitor": "ner_f1, hallucination_rate"}. If monitor breaches thresholds, traffic automatically shifts back to pinned version.
- Auto-fallback policy: we can create a metric-hook that compares live NER_F1 (sampled) to baseline every 15 minutes; if absolute drop > 2%, traffic shifts to fallback and an alert page is triggered. We’ll include the webhook and runbook in rollback-playbook.pdf.

Timeline and next steps:
- Today: sending artifacts (attached).
- 48 hours: Redwood runs the eval pack against your full sample and shares an annotated report.
- Day 3: joint tech call to review detailed diffs and pick initial model + canary config.
- Trial: 2-week POC with canary at 10% for first 72 hours, then ramp to 50% if metrics stable.

SOC2 & compliance: Sean, I’ll drop the link to our compliance packet in the thread (and share with procurement).

Notes for operations (config snippet):
- Pin example: project:novatech -> model: redwood-llama3-13b-int8 -> version: 1.3.0
- Canary example: route: novatech-infer -> canary.percent = 10 -> monitor.metrics = [ner_f1, hallucination_rate] -> rollback.threshold.ner_f1 = -2.0

If this aligns I’ll schedule the tech review for Fri morning PST.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: novatech-eval-benchmarks-20270421.csv (CSV), prompt-set-novatech-v1.json (JSON), rollback-playbook.pdf (PDF)
